messages:
marco: Heads-up - i'm doing a pass on the migration guide for audit exports and noticed inconsistent SDK snippets for retention and an example that includes a raw prompt. we should fix before merge.

elaine: thanks for catching. what variants do we have today?

marco: node uses `expires_at`, py has `ttl_seconds`, and the go snippet currently shows `prompt_text: '...'`.

ops: yikes on `prompt_text`. that could teach users bad hygiene.

legal: SOC2 guidance: avoid absolute language. prefer 'retained for N days' and explicitly mention legal hold or investigation exceptions. also don't show raw user content in public docs.

elaine: propose we standardize on `retention_period_days` (int) in all snippets and add a short callout: "Values are subject to legal hold and export approval."

marco: agree. i'd also like to add a tiny migration note in the guide that maps old field names to the canonical one to help customers migrating SDK versions. simple table: expires_at -> retention_period_days, ttl_seconds -> retention_period_days.

ops: please also update the API reference table on audit-exports to match the snippet names. otherwise engineers get confused.

legal: please include wording: "Do not include raw prompt text in examples. Use pseudonymized ids (e.g., prompt_id: \"p_...\") and document the audited admin flow to retrieve originals when authorized."

elaine: i'll open a PR that: 1) replaces field names across JS/Py/Go/Ruby snippets, 2) replaces raw prompt examples with `prompt_id` pseudonymization, 3) adds migration mapping note, and 4) updates the audit-exports field table.

devex-bot: PR #4271 created by elaine: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4271 - "docs: harmonize retention field names; pseudonymize prompt examples; migration mapping"

marco: thanks. can you also add a one-line automated check (docs lint) that flags `prompt_text:` occurrences in examples? that would prevent regressions.

elaine: good idea. i'll add a simple grep-based check in CI and include it in the PR.

ops: security nit - in the migration note, remind users to verify timezone conversions if they consumed `expires_at` before. converting ISO expirations to days can be lossy.

legal: final check from my side once PR lands. i'll review wording for SOC2 compliance.

marco: perfect. small coordinated changes but high impact for compliance and dev clarity. thanks everyone.
